title: Replace a hand written converter with a MapStruct mapper
summary: OrderMapper moves to MapStruct, customerName quietly turns null, and unmappedTargetPolicy makes the build catch it.

turns.user: i'm tired of editing OrderMapper by hand every time a field shows up. can we do mapstruct? needs to be injectable as a spring bean

assistant.body: Great choice. MapStruct generates the implementation at compile time, so there is no reflection and it runs as fast as the hand written version. With componentModel = "spring" the generated OrderMapperImpl carries @Component, and you keep injecting it through the constructor as before. Properties with the same name are matched for you, so only the renamed one, number to orderNumber, needs a @Mapping. The enum to String conversion for status is built in, and customerName gets filled from customer.name automatically.

turns.user: swapped it in. customerName comes back null on every order. no error, nothing

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. MapStruct only matches properties whose names are equal. It never splits customerName into customer and name to go looking. A target property with no source falls under unmappedTargetPolicy, which defaults to WARN, so all you got was an Unmapped target property warning in the compile output and a null at runtime. A nested value is written with a dot in source. Setting the policy to ERROR turns the next miss like this into a failed build instead of a silent null.

turns.user: build fails now. Unmapped target property: "shippedAt". right, i added shippedAt to OrderResponse. on Order it is called dispatchedAt. null is fine if it has not shipped yet

assistant.body: That is ERROR doing exactly its job. Under WARN, shippedAt would have been null forever without a word. One more line maps it from dispatchedAt. An order that has not shipped has a null dispatchedAt, which carries over as a null shippedAt, so there is no need to silence it with ignore = true.
